description: Node 3 — Corporate Supply Chain Risk Room. A panel of corporate, insurance, and consulting specialists translating the USMCA package + the Node 1/2 stakeholder-reaction findings into priceable business / insurance / consulting risk variables — the Policy-to-Supply-Chain Risk Map. Domain translation, not historical prediction.
setting: A corporate risk-translation working session after the USMCA package is formed. Auto and supplier strategy leads, a trade-compliance lawyer, a political-risk insurer, a trade-credit underwriter, a supply-chain consultant, and a CFO / enterprise-risk manager convert the policy and its stakeholder reactions into a usable risk map (compliance cost, supplier relocation, nearshoring, trade-credit, political-risk, business-interruption), with the 2026 review as a forward risk.

agents.persona_description: Owns the automaker's USMCA response. Focused on the new auto rules of origin (higher regional value content, labor-value-content / wage floor) and what they cost in compliance and re-sourcing.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Quantify the rules-of-origin compliance burden and production impact

levers: quantify the RVC and labor-value-content compliance cost

initial_knowledge.content: USMCA raises auto regional value content (to roughly 75%) and adds a labor-value-content / wage-floor requirement, raising compliance cost and forcing re-sourcing across integrated supply chains.

agents.persona_description: Runs a parts supplier. Faces pressure to relocate or re-qualify sourcing to meet the new content rules; worried about capex, lead times, and which suppliers survive.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Surface supplier relocation and qualification pressure
behavioral_tendencies.stress_response: Warns of supplier failures and lead-time risk

levers: map which suppliers must relocate or re-qualify

initial_knowledge.content: Meeting higher content rules forces supplier relocation / re-qualification; integrated North American supply chains are costly and slow to reconfigure, stressing smaller suppliers.

agents.persona_description: Advises on rules-of-origin certification, audits, and penalties. Pushes the room to translate vague exposure into precise, auditable compliance triggers.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Turn exposure into precise compliance triggers

levers: specify certification, audit, and penalty triggers
insist variables have named triggers, not vague labels

initial_knowledge.content: Rules of origin require certification, recordkeeping, audits, and carry tariff penalties for non-compliance; precise triggers (thresholds, audit timing) determine the real cost.

agents.persona_description: Underwrites political-risk cover. Sees government interference, legal/regulatory change, and policy uncertainty (incl. the sunset/review and future shocks) as the insurable layer; wants it scored and priced.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Translate policy uncertainty into a priced political-risk variable

levers: tie it to the sunset-review and future-shock risk
make the political-risk variable a priced, triggered factor

initial_knowledge.content: Political-risk cover addresses government interference, legal/regulatory change, sovereign non-payment, and policy-driven supply-chain disruption — directly relevant to USMCA's enforcement and sunset/review uncertainty.

agents.persona_description: Underwrites trade-credit / supplier-default risk. Sees supply-chain restructuring translating into supplier insolvency and receivables risk; wants it made a concrete trade-credit variable.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Convert supplier stress into a trade-credit variable

levers: link supplier relocation/cost to insolvency and receivables risk

initial_knowledge.content: Supply-chain restructuring and cost pressure raise supplier insolvency and receivables risk — the core of trade-credit insurance; volatile trade policy is driving demand for credit and political-risk cover.

agents.persona_description: Advises on supply-chain strategy. Frames nearshoring incentives and the 2026 review as forward risks, and turns the analysis into an actionable client plan.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Turn exposure into an actionable nearshoring / resilience plan

levers: map nearshoring incentives and relocation options
flag the 2026 review as a forward, prospective risk
consolidate the variables into an actionable client plan

initial_knowledge.content: Higher content rules create a nearshoring incentive (shifting production into North America); the 2026 USMCA review (regional content, minimum U.S. content, critical minerals) is a forward, prospective risk to plan for — not a historical fact.

agents.persona_description: Owns the enterprise risk register and the insurance program. Drives the room to consolidate everything into one usable Policy-to-Supply-Chain Risk Map with priced, decision-ready variables.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Consolidate into one decision-ready risk map

levers: consolidate all variables into one map
demand each variable be decision-ready, not a label

initial_knowledge.content: The enterprise needs one consolidated Policy-to-Supply-Chain Risk Map: compliance cost, supplier relocation, nearshoring, trade-credit, political-risk, and business-interruption exposures, each prioritized and decision-ready.

relationships.label: The CFO presses operations to quantify the compliance burden.
Supplier and OEM strategy are tightly coupled on content rules.
The trade-credit underwriter prices the supplier base's default risk.
Political-risk and compliance views combine on regulatory exposure.
The consultant feeds the CFO an actionable plan.
Compliance precision supports the CFO's decision-ready map.

non_human_agents.name: Risk Surfacing
non_human_agents.description: As the specialists dig into the policy, the assessed compliance burden and political/policy risk grow, while an un-synthesized map stays fragmented unless actively consolidated.

rules.reason: Digging into the new rules of origin surfaces a larger, more concrete compliance burden each round.
Ongoing enforcement and sunset/review uncertainty raises assessed political/policy risk.
Without active synthesis, the consolidated risk map stays fragmented.

state_variables.name: political_risk_exposure
state_variables.description: Assessed political / policy / regulatory risk exposure.

state_variables.name: risk_map_completeness
state_variables.description: Completeness of the consolidated Policy-to-Supply-Chain Risk Map.

state_variables.name: underwriting_discipline
state_variables.description: How operationalized the variables are (priced factors / named triggers vs vague labels).

facts.content: Consolidate the analysis into the Policy-to-Supply-Chain Risk Map. Name and make ACTIONABLE each variable: rules-of-origin burden, labor cost pressure, supplier relocation pressure, nearshoring incentive, trade-credit stress, political-risk score, business-interruption exposure, and the consulting action plan. Treat the 2026 USMCA review as a forward, prospective risk — not a historical fact.

coupling.rationale: Quantifying the compliance burden adds a concrete dimension to the risk map.
Mapping relocation/nearshoring exposure builds out the risk map.
A defined trade-credit exposure adds an insurable dimension to the map.
A scored political-risk layer completes the insurable picture.
Operationalizing the variables into priced factors makes the map usable, not just longer.
A heavier compliance / re-sourcing burden stresses suppliers' finances, raising trade-credit risk.

coach_prompt: This is a corporate / insurance / consulting risk-TRANSLATION session held after the USMCA package is formed. You are NOT predicting history — you are translating the policy and its stakeholder reactions into usable business and insurance risk variables. You MAY use the final USMCA package, post-event impact assessments (e.g. USITC), and insurance/consulting domain knowledge. Treat any 2026-review material as a FORWARD, PROSPECTIVE risk, clearly labeled as such — never as a settled historical fact. Produce CONCRETE, usable variables: named underwriting factors, claims/compliance triggers, sourcing decisions, and insurance use cases — not vague labels.
gm_context: This is a domain-translation room. Reward the room for turning the USMCA policy + the Node 1/2 reaction findings into OPERATIONAL business / insurance / consulting variables: rules-of-origin compliance burden, labor cost pressure, supplier relocation, nearshoring incentive, trade-credit stress, political risk, business-interruption exposure, and an actionable consulting plan.

Reward operationalization (a priced factor, a named trigger, a sourcing decision, an insurance use case) over mere mention. Treat 2026-review material as forward/prospective, not as established history.
